paragraphs.text: As a result of the above, the Appellants felt they were targeted because they were Chinese, much more than businesses owned by native Guyanese. The Appellants submit that the police in Guyana cannot protect Chinese businesses or Chinese people and that there was a lot of corruption among the police in Guyana

The Appellants submit, in spite of their credible allegations, the RPD determined that they were not Convention refugees, because of a lack of nexus to a Convention ground. They submit that the RPD erred in finding that they were not targeted in Guyana because of their Chinese ethnicity, but were merely victims of criminal acts directed at business owners. The Appellant further submits that the RPD failed to properly consider the evidence supporting their well-founded fear of persecution based on their Chinese ethnicity. The Appellants referred to new evidence submitted to the RAD, evidence that was rejected according to section 110(4) of IRPA.

The Appellants submit that objective country wide documentation supports the above submission, albeit there is not a vast amount of objective evidence because the ethnic minorities make up a small portion of the Guyanese population. The Appellants disclosed an article from October 13, 201517 regarding the armed robbery of a Chinese restaurant owner. Citing other documentation, referenced below, the Appellants rejected the RPD's finding that rejects the article because a close associate of the victim made this statement. The Appellants also submit that the RPD failed to consider the balance of the article that outlines further attacks against Chinese nationals.

The Appellants submitted further articles that described how other Chinese nationals are targeted by gunmen.18 They submit that this evidence corroborates their subjective belief that they were targeted because of their Chinese ethnicity.

The Appellants referred to the RPD decision, paragraph 16,19 where it states, "...when protection was sought, the police may have been influenced by racism." They submit that the RPD found this racism to be relevant to the issue of nexus, because it speaks only to the motivations of the police, not the motives for the actual crimes that were carried out against them. The Appellants submit that this finding is unsustainable in law.
The Appellants did not specifically address this issue on appeal.

The Appellants submit that the RPD failed to appreciate that the risk faced by the Appellants sufficiently particularized such that they are not excluded from the definition of, "persons in need of protection." According to the Appellants, the critical factor is the risk they face is personalized because of the racism of the police. They further submit that the risk faced by the Appellants submits that the Chinese is distinctly different from the general risks faced by all Guyana.

The Appellants quoted federal jurisprudence to submit that the fact that because the risk that they face has its genesis in criminal activity does not in itself mean that the risk is one generally faced by others in Guyana.25 The Appellants submit that the RPD erred in finding that they face a generalized risk in Guyana.
